title: Gamliel of Kuntiya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: (Kuntiya is a place-name.) At the end of Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim, chapter 10, Rabbi Mana went up to release Gamliel of Kuntiya from a vow. Later he released Gamliel’s grandson, also named Gamliel. Seder HaDorot incorrectly copied this as Rabban Gamliel, Rabbi Mana’s grandson.

Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3:5, 12b, relates that when Gamliel of Kuntiya died, the people of Kursai buried him among themselves. Three days later they decided to bring him back for burial in his own place and consulted Rabbi Simon. This shows that he lived in the second and third generations.

notes.text: The two Gamli’els are grandfather and grandson, not Rabbi Mana and his grandson. The checked burial passage reads Bursai where Hyman supplies Kursai. “Bring him back” is a verb, not a people called Hazara.

The inspected Nedarim passage distinguishes the two Gamliels as grandfather and grandson. The assignment to the second and third generations remains Hyman’s inference from the passages, not an independently established chronology.
